key_insight: Tuning inter-nanoparticle repulsion produces four self-organized morphologies—droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed—with distinct effects on polymer ordering.
engineering_relevance: Inter-nanoparticle repulsion offers a potential design lever for controlling morphology and polymer alignment in strongly confined polymer nanocomposites.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of a compact nanoparticle droplet in a semiflexible, rod-like polymer matrix under extreme confinement.
Varied nanoparticle–nanoparticle repulsion while holding other interactions fixed.
Used cluster analysis and descriptors of nanoparticle crystallinity and polymer nematic order.
evidence_signal: The slab regime showed the strongest polymer nematic order despite negligible nanoparticle crystallization, whereas crystalline droplets reduced nematic order and dispersed nanoparticles enabled local smectic-like ordering.
watch_item: Results apply to the simulated, extremely confined system; transfer to bulk materials or experimental formulations requires validation.
paper_title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
